recognizability_levers.summary: high part count, low type variety; reserve for one focal accent; ~1200 parts/m^3; budget vs ~4-5k flicker ceiling
low count, high type variety (~54% unique); recognizability from a few signature silhouette parts + cheap interior variety
replica reads via correct proportions + standard feature placement + per-instance color on identical parts, not part variety
solidity/smoothness = part count at fixed envelope+scale; add segments, don't enlarge
radial short-wall ribs chained to ONE apex make the cleanest spire; doubling rib count closes inter-rib gaps; half-scale walls + tighter base = tall pointy spire
SET_CLASS_A/B/S are geometry-identical, color-only (magenta/blue/gold); a beam cone is freely recolored or mixed by swapping the emitter
close a floating base gap by snapping the same part to the drum and angling it OPPOSITE the spire (chevron); same-angle extension reads unfinished

S_LARGETRYE0 is a fan/star vault, not a pyramid; never use it as a clean finial point
facet tilt about the tangent: negative=inward=clean cone; positive/radial-outset=outward=spiky

orientation_recipes.lean: base Euler(90,0,a+90); rotate phi about tangent t=(-sin a, cos a, 0). NEGATIVE phi = inward (clean cone); positive = outward (spiky).
orientation_recipes.aim_at_apex: vertical at azimuth a; tilt by -atan(radius/apex_height) about the tangent so the axis converges on the apex point.
orientation_recipes.rib_aim: basis columns (d, up x d, d x (up x d)) with d=(apex-base).normalized(); the part's LOCAL X maps to d; chain copies along d for length.
orientation_recipes.api_quirk: BUILDER.add_part(id) templates; .duplicate() returns an UNLINKED object - must collection.objects.link(obj) or it will not render.

placement_recipes.note: ribs chained to one apex; double rib_count to close gaps; half-scale + tighter base = tall pointy spire
single rim ring tilted to one apex = true converging light cone; density = ring spacing
snap to the drum top; counter the spire's lean to close a floating base gap
tile between ribs with scale variation + azimuth stagger for overlap texture
truncate facets BEFORE convergence; cap with a single un-stacked piece; anti-swirl

fit_rules: ring z-spacing <= facet vertical extent (else tier gaps)
facet width <= base circumference / facet count (else chaotic overlap; N=8 octagon min for _M walls)
truncate a lower cone stage WIDE before a collar (else the upper stage collapses)
solidity/smoothness = part count at a fixed envelope and scale; add segments, do not enlarge (finding 19)
live_build_disciplines: screenshot-verify every build step before continuing
checkpoint-save the .blend / export through the add-on after each batch (a crash resets the live scene to default)
live creative geometry is BLENDER-tier, not GAME_VALIDATED

members.role: circular macro room / rotunda / topper mass
square macro room / penthouse block / pod / roof adapter

rules: Use as structural fabric, not decoration.
Do not only stack rooms vertically.
Create distinct silhouettes through offsets, pods, overhangs, bridges, receivers, cranes, dishes, and layered modules.
Attach antennas/spires to visible mounts or room tops.
Use color deliberately for function/district identity.
Avoid repeating red lens band + antenna crown + stacked room as the default topper pattern.
failure_modes: topper not integrated to roof interface
validation: check all antennas/details visibly mount to room geometry

members.role: cargo rack / conveyor cassette / machine module

rules: Robotic arms require visible mounts and a target task.
Conveyor/cargo parts must read as cassettes, racks, rails, or machine modules.
Repeated conveyor modules must use consistent orientation and spacing.
Drone hives need visible docking collars, service bays, or wall racks.
Avoid sparse robot parts on a pad.
known_issues: B_WALL_CARG1 orientation can read as random barrels if no rails/cassette context is provided.
Robot arms look toy-like without mounts and task targets.
Hive drone parts look loose unless connected by service struts/collars.

rules: Antennas/spires must be mounted to visible bases, pylons, rooms, scaffolds, or tower caps.
Do not float antennas high above a structure unless the design explicitly includes a holographic suspension system.
Antenna crowns need a named function: broadcast, scanner, docking guidance, defense, weather, relay, or AI-control signal.
Vary height and role when many antennas are used, but keep them structurally connected.
failure_modes: generic antenna crowns with no role
